problem: Given the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+2y \\ 4y+3x\end{aligned}],$ find  $2\cdot \text{nullity}(T)-1.$
worked_solution:
First, we write down the standard matrix of $T:$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Recall that $\text{nullity}(T)=\text{nullity}(T)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(T)).$

In order to find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(T)),$ we reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has no non-pivot column. Therefore, $\text{nullity}(T)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(T))=0.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
2\cdot \text{nullity}(T)-1=2\cdot 0-1=-1.
$$
